item.title: Sixty galleries from SF and around the world strut their stuff at the intimate 'Fog Design + Art Fair'.
item.description: People love Fog Design + Art, one of San Francisco’s biggest art fairs, for a lot of reasons: the quality of the galleries, the work, the scale—which is more intimate than sprawling fairs such as Art Basel Miami—and the location, spread over two piers at Mason.“I mean, we’re not under a tent in South Beach,” says Mariah Nielson, the founder of the gallery and research center Blunk Space, who appreciates the light in the exhibition hall and the view of Alcatraz and the bay. item.description: An adorable gift shop for cat-crazy customers, two restaurants devoted to slinky soba noodles, a coffee shop whose lattes boast Okinawan black sugar, and a neighborhood store overflowing with cool vintage t-shirts and vinyl. item.title: The Big Art Loop is transforming SF into an open air gallery over the next three years.
item.description: On a clear afternoon along the waterfront, R-Evolution rises in front of the Ferry Building with quiet confidence. Facing the city, it stands as a marker of resilience and renewal, a reminder that San Francisco’s identity extends beyond technology to the creativity expressed through art. That sensibility defines the Big Art Loop, a project built on a simple and surprisingly radical idea: art does not need walls. item.title: 10 Old-School Restaurants for Classic SF Vibes
item.description: San Francisco has a rightful place in the history books—from faces and historic places to shaky ground and iconic sounds, from the rowdy sailors of the Barbary Coast to the peaceful voices of the counterculture movement. item.title: Celebrate 25 Years of Lunar New Year at OMCA
item.description: The Oakland Museum of California (OMCA) is inviting the Bay Area to celebrate a major milestone: the 25th Annual Lunar New Year Celebration. One of OMCA’s most beloved traditions, this full-day, family-friendly festival on Saturday, February 21st, honors the holiday and uplifts Asian American and Pacific Islander communities across the region through vibrant performances, hands-on activities, storytelling, and food. item.title: Locals We Love: Documentary photographer Ashima Yadava democratizes art through collaboration.
item.description: Most documentary photographs tell only one version of a story, the perspective captured by an outsider looking in.But people aren’t so one-dimensional. item.title: 5 Romantic Couples Baths Near San Francisco to Soak Up the Love, Together
item.description: There’s something so relaxing about getting into a hot bath, letting the warm water ease the stress away. And when you can share a bath with your partner, you both come away feeling reset, recharged, and reconnected. From day spas with a view to mineral mud baths to splurge getaways with private hot tubs, there’s no better way to bond than with a romantic couples soak.Monterey Plaza Hotel & Spa, MontereyFrom the private spa suite at the Vista Blue Spa on the top floor of the Monterey Plaza Hotel
